PLANNER EXCEPTIONS (authoring:onemessagebus-plan): all seven refused criteria replaced in their own tasks; the eight passed tasks are byte-identical (sha256 verified); `just check-plan` refuses only the five missing review records and the unregistered onemessagebus repository. Four decisions were made without a ruling, each recorded in the task and in the project record's new "second criteria repair" section:
1) The brief said `events emit` applies "whichever rule Contract W assigns to the event envelope", but Contract W assigned none. I assigned the emitter `bound_payload` (head-keeping, `truncated: true` stamp), because that is where onevcs::stream (`bound()` at emit) and onepipeline::journal (`within_the_bound` at relay) apply it today, and oneagentgraph's tail-keeping `bound_text` is applied in its typed payload builders before the map reaches its emitter, so a compliant oneagentgraph payload passes the bus emitter unchanged with no stamp. onevcs-adopt-bus (passed, untouched) already says its Stream keeps no payload-bound of its own, which is consistent only with this assignment.
2) Contract C's family rule in bus-scaffold-wire-core was reworded from "never as an argv word" to "never as a positional argument", with `deliver --message` named as the permitted named-option form, so the rule and the `--message` ruling read the same. bus-inbox-notes' Contract C now says exactly one of stdin / `--file` / `--message` is given; what happens when two are given is left to the worker.
3) The per-source write version proof goes through `events emit --source <word>` for the three profile source words, assuming the binary's `events` verbs apply the agent profile the binary links (Contract C gives `events merge` a `--profile` default; `events emit` gained no flag).
4) ai-orchestrator-adopt-bus-releases' host-install criterion is split: the cached tier of tests/test_host_installs.py is the bar; the committed fixture tests/fixtures/release-targets/onemessagebus.toml is held to the four targets bus-scaffold-wire-core declares (corresponding-content shape), with the `reads_checkouts` tier (`orchestrator:test-checkouts`) named as the later check and not the bar.
No contract's shape moved; no node, edge, decision or follow-up changed.

Planner (onemessagebus-repair-2), batched questions on the four forks I decided without a ruling while repairing the 7 refused criteria; each is applied in the plan now and I will move it to your answer.

1) EMITTER BOUNDING RULE. Your ruling said 'events emit applies whichever rule Contract W assigns to the event envelope', but Contract W assigned none. I assigned the emitter (Emitter::emit, and so events emit) the head-keeping bound_payload rule with the 'truncated: true' stamp, because onevcs::stream applies exactly that at emit and onepipeline::journal at relay, while oneagentgraph applies its tail-keeping bound_text inside typed payload builders before the map reaches its emitter (so a compliant oneagentgraph payload passes the bus emitter unchanged, no stamp). onevcs-adopt-bus (passed, untouched) already says its Stream keeps no payload-bound of its own, which only works under this assignment. Confirm bound_payload as the emitter's rule? (Alternative: the emitter bounds nothing and every producer bounds before emit — that would move onevcs-adopt-bus, a passed task.)

2) PER-SOURCE WRITE VERSION THROUGH THE BINARY. To prove 'pipeline writes v:2, agentgraph/vcs write v:1' through a real interface, the criterion uses 'events emit --source <word>' for the three profile words and assumes the binary's events verbs run under the agent profile the binary links (Contract C gives events merge an optional --profile; events emit has no such flag). Accept that assumption as stated, or should Contract C give events emit a --profile <name> option too (default: the agent profile), so a profile is chosen the same way on both events verbs?

3) DELIVER'S THREE SOURCES. Contract C in bus-inbox-notes now says the message comes from stdin, --file, or the named --message option, exactly one of the three; the criterion proves each works and that a second positional after <address> is refused. It does not say what happens when two sources are given at once. Leave that to the worker, or state 'more than one source given is refused naming both'?

4) HOST-INSTALL FIXTURE SHAPE. ai-orchestrator-adopt-bus-releases' refused criterion is split: the cached tier of tests/test_host_installs.py is the bar; the committed tests/fixtures/release-targets/onemessagebus.toml is a corresponding-content criterion held to the four targets bus-scaffold-wire-core declares (crate:onemessagebus as crate, crate:onemessagebus-agent as agent-crate, pypi:onemessagebus-cli as pypi, npm:onemessagebus-cli as npm), with the reads_checkouts tier (orchestrator:test-checkouts) named as the later check whose result is not the bar. Is naming the four ids literally in the criterion right, or should it say only 'every target the released declaration declares and no other', leaving the ids to be read off the registered checkout?

Everything else in the plan is unchanged; check-plan refuses only the review records and the unregistered repository.
